guides.wedding-stationery-set-maker.titl: Wedding Stationery: What You Actually Need on the Day
guides.wedding-stationery-set-maker.desc: A practical wedding stationery checklist from invitations through menus, place cards and signage, with print sizes and what you can safely skip.
guides.wedding-stationery-set-maker.lead: Most stationery falls into three groups: before the day, guest-facing on the day, and operational. The third group is the one people forget.
guides.wedding-stationery-set-maker.f2v: Order of service, menus, place cards, table numbers, signage
guides.wedding-stationery-set-maker.f3v: Vendor timeline, meal-choice list, seating map, emergency contacts
guides.wedding-stationery-set-maker.f4v: Match a single card stock and ink colour across pieces
guides.wedding-stationery-set-maker.s1: Design one small system — a typeface pair, two colours and one motif — then apply it everywhere instead of designing each item separately. List every piece with a quantity and a deadline, and add 10% overprint for place cards and menus because names change. Print the operational sheets separately; they are for the coordinator, not the guests, and should be easy to update.
guides.wedding-stationery-set-maker.s2: US stationery suites often include a details card, a registry card and a separate RSVP card with its own stamped envelope. UK and European suites more commonly use a folded card with a single reply address, and an order of service is standard for a church ceremony. Standard sizes differ too — A5 and A6 are common in Europe, while US pieces use inch dimensions such as 5 × 7 — so check the lab's templates before designing.
guides.wedding-stationery-set-maker.s3: Do not print place cards before RSVPs close, and do not use the same wording for a ceremony programme and a reception menu. Check that any religious text is approved by the officiant before printing. Order envelopes with the rest of the suite so the stock matches, and keep a digital master of every piece for last-minute corrections.
guides.wedding-stationery-set-maker.a1: Invitations, a way to reply, and a clear schedule for guests. Menus, programmes, place cards and signage are useful but optional depending on the format.
guides.wedding-stationery-set-maker.q2: How many spare place cards should we print?
guides.wedding-stationery-set-maker.a2: About 10% extra, and keep a few blanks plus a matching pen for day-of changes.
guides.wedding-stationery-set-maker.q3: When should on-the-day stationery go to print?
guides.wedding-stationery-set-maker.a3: After RSVPs close and menu choices are final, typically two to three weeks before the wedding.
